---
title: "check-local-macros.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags LaTeX macros defined outside
[`Morrison-Lab/macros`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/macros).
The lab's rule is that new macros go only in that repository,
never in an applied repository,
unless the repository explicitly overrides
one specific macro the library already has.
This is check 2 of
[gha#1077](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1077);
check 1 is [`check-literal-math-letters`](check-literal-math-letters.qmd).

The check flags a definition command on a line a pull request adds:
`\newcommand`, `\renewcommand`, `\providecommand`, `\DeclareMathOperator`,
`\DeclarePairedDelimiter`, `\DeclareRobustCommand`,
`\NewDocumentCommand` and its relatives, and the TeX primitives
`\def`, `\gdef`, `\edef` and `\xdef`.
It reads `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, `.md`, `.tex`, `.sty`, `.cls` and `.html` files,
the last because a MathJax header file can define macros.
Each finding names the macro being defined.

The check does not flag:

- a code fence or code span in a Markdown-family file,
  except a fence whose language is `tex`, `latex`, or a raw
  `{=tex}`, `{=latex}` or `{=html}` block,
  which is where a Quarto page keeps definitions;
- an HTML comment or YAML front matter;
- a `%` comment in a `.tex`, `.sty` or `.cls` file;
- a line carrying, or following, `<!-- check-local-macros: allow -->`.

## Override files

A file matching `override-files` (default `macros-override.*`)
may redefine only a macro the library already defines.
The library's names are read from the files in `library`,
for example the `latex-macros` submodule's `macros.qmd`
(set `submodules: true` so the reusable workflow checks it out).
A definition in an override file is allowed
when the library defines the same name,
and flagged when it does not.
With no `library`, the names cannot be checked,
and the run warns how many override definitions it left unchecked
instead of reporting them clean.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so a repository's existing local macros are not reflagged
on every unrelated edit.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose,
for example to list the local macros a repository still carries.

Every run prints how many lines, files and definitions it examined.

## Limitations

- A definition split over several lines is found by its command,
  so the name is read only when it follows the command on the same line.
  A definition whose name is on the next line is reported without a name.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.
- The check cannot tell a macro that duplicates a library macro from a new one
  outside an override file; the rule is that all of them belong in the library.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.Rmd *.md *.tex *.sty *.cls *.html'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `override-files` | string  | `'**/macros-override.*,macros-override.*'` | Glob patterns naming override files. |
| `library`        | string  | `''`    | Space-separated paths of library files whose definitions are the names an override may redefine. |
| `submodules`     | string  | `'false'` | Passed to `actions/checkout`, so a library submodule is available. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `false` | Fail the workflow when a macro defined outside the library is found. Warn-only by default. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | `'ubuntu-latest'` | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-local-macros.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags LaTeX macros defined on lines a PR adds
# (`\newcommand`, `\def`, `\DeclareMathOperator`, ...), because new macros belong
# in Morrison-Lab/macros. Warn-only by default. A `macros-override.*` file may
# redefine only a macro the library already has; pass `library` to check that.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check macros defined outside the library

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-local-macros.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.tex *.sty'             # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   submodules: true                       # check out the latex-macros submodule ...
    #   library: 'latex-macros/macros.qmd'     # ... and check overrides against it
    #   fail: true                             # block instead of warn (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-local-macros.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-local-macros.yml)
for the full caller stub.
